blocks.passage:
A cross-border transaction is any deal where the buyer and the seller are in different countries. It looks like a normal sale, but many small extras appear along the way.

You will pay for shipping. You will pay customs. You will lose a little in the currency exchange. There may be a small bank fee. None of these are huge, but together they change the price.

The lesson is simple: always check the real cost of a cross-border deal, not just the invoice price.

items.q: What is a cross-border transaction?
options: A deal where buyer and seller are in different countries
items.why: "any deal where the buyer and the seller are in different countries."

items.q: Which is one of the 'small extras' the text lists?
items.why: "You will pay for shipping."

items.q: What do the extras do together?
items.why: "together they change the price."

items.q: What is the simple lesson?
options: Only look at the invoice price
Always check the real cost, not just the invoice price
items.why: "always check the real cost of a cross-border deal, not just the invoice price."

items.q: Why does the text say to check the real cost?
options: Because the invoice price hides the extras
items.why: Inferência: os extras não aparecem no preço da fatura, mas somam-se a ele.

audio.text:
You saw a supplier's price of one thousand euros and thought 'that's the cost'. But when the goods arrived, it had become one thousand and eighty. Let me show you where the extra eighty came from — none of it is a surprise once you know.

Start with the invoice: one thousand euros for the goods. That's the number everyone remembers.

Then, shipping. Getting the goods to you cost thirty euros. That's on top.

Then, a small customs duty at the border — say twenty euros.

Then, the currency exchange. You paid in euros but your account is in another currency, and you lost a little in the conversion — about twenty euros.

And finally, a small bank fee for the international payment — ten euros.

Thirty, plus twenty, plus twenty, plus ten. That's eighty euros of extras. So the real, landed cost is one thousand and eighty, not one thousand.

None of these are big on their own. But if you plan on the invoice price alone, your margin quietly disappears. Always add up the landed cost first.

items.q: What was the supplier's invoice price?
items.why: "a supplier's price of one thousand euros."

items.q: How much did shipping add?
items.why: "Getting the goods to you cost thirty euros."

items.q: Why did the currency exchange add a cost?
options: You paid in euros but your account is in another currency, losing a little in conversion
items.why: "you lost a little in the conversion — about twenty euros."

items.q: What is the real, landed cost?
items.why: "the real, landed cost is one thousand and eighty, not one thousand."

items.q: What happens if you plan on the invoice price alone?
items.why: "if you plan on the invoice price alone, your margin quietly disappears."

items.q: A **cross-border** transaction is…
items.why: Cross-border = transfronteiriço.

items.q: The **landed cost** is…
options: the total real cost including shipping, duty, fees and exchange
items.why: Landed cost = custo total no destino.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A **bank ___** is charged for the international payment."
items.why: Bank fee = tarifa bancária.

items.q: An **exchange loss** happens when…
options: you lose value converting one currency to another
items.why: Exchange loss = perda na conversão de moeda.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "These costs are **___** — they don't show on the invoice."
items.why: Hidden = ocultos.

items.q: "Shipping is **on top of** the price." On top of means…
items.why: On top of = além de, somado a.

items.q: "Let's **add up** the extras." To add up means to…
items.why: Add up = somar.

items.q: "The extras **pile up** quickly." To pile up means to…
items.why: Pile up = acumular-se.

items.q: "Your margin can **quietly disappear**." Quietly disappear means…
items.why: Quietly disappear = sumir sem se perceber.

items.q: "Always **factor in** the extras." To factor in means to…
items.why: Factor in = levar em conta.
